author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: At 00:00 UTC on 15 February 2022 markets are pricing two shocks at once: a Fed pushed toward a faster March lift-off by 7.5% CPI (2Y 1.58%, +59 bps over 20 observations, a bear flattening of a positively sloped curve) and a Russia-Ukraine invasion window (Brent 96.48 USD/bbl, VIX 28.33, gold 1,869.40 USD/oz, STOXX 600 -1.83% on 2022-02-14). The call is to keep equity beta below benchmark, fund energy, gold and defence hedges from long duration and long-duration growth, underweight Europe and Poland most, and prefer commodity exporters (Australia, materials) and pricing-power franchises until diplomacy in Moscow or a softer Fed path lowers the premia.
sources_policy: Facts come only from the 2022-02-15 frozen feed (tools/digest.py) and the 2022-02-15 market card (tools/showcard.py / cards/2022-02-15.json). Every number is a card value quoted exactly or appears in a headline cited in the same part. Every cited ID was re-checked against its own-date headline text and timestamp (strictly before 2022-02-15T00:00Z, inside the 7/14/35-day windows), and every quoted card value was re-checked directly against cards/2022-02-15.json after the root's scratch-isolation warning. Previews are used only for pending events and never for outcomes. Company results are kept separate from previews. Each citation is used at most twice: 257 distinct IDs, 279 uses. There are no spot-FX levels or returns; currency direction comes only from dated reporting (zloty) or general rate-differential mechanics (yen), and DXY is the only dollar measure quoted. Period identities follow the card names: Meta Platforms (FB), Raytheon Technologies (RTX), Digital World Acquisition (DWAC), Mercedes-Benz Group, Schlumberger. No Polish companies appear in the Sector Deep Dive. The exclusions file for the date lists none.

Promotional or low-quality items omitted: n0898 Grizzle lithium 'catch-up trade', n0795 OilPrice '5 Hot Small Cap Oil And Gas Stocks', n0352 'Metaverse Stocks to Buy', Motley Fool Shiba Inu return pieces (n0955, n0939), n1754 'dollar supply up 411%'.
n1739 Newsweek Polska allegation about missing Russian-bank files at the NBP involving Glapiński: an unverified allegation not needed for the analysis; omitted.
Stale previews superseded by outcomes: n0379 (SoftBank earnings preview), n1636 and n1644 (Polish MPC decision previews); omitted.

Known-but-unevidenced events: Japan Q4 GDP (released 23:50 UTC on 14 February) and Canada's Emergencies Act invocation (14 February evening) have no own-date headline, so neither is mentioned. The Super Bowl ads (known) are used through own-date headlines.

Pending events with no dated preview: US January PPI, the RBA minutes (00:30 UTC on 15 February) and Airbnb, Roblox and Upstart results are not dated or described; the five-session run-ups in UPST, RBLX and ABNB are cited only as card moves 'ahead of their next prints'. The Scholz-Putin meeting, Munich Security Conference outcomes and the EU rule-of-law judgment are treated as pending with no outcome.

n1328 Reuters 'ECB to raise deposit rate to -0.25% by year-end' is a forecast-type item and is written as an expectation only. n0883 TipRanks is used only to establish a notable earnings slate, with no company dates inferred from it. n0233 Reuters Insight is cited as 'a Trump deal' without naming its parties beyond the headline.
